  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well
as states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of California, and a
federal emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading
COVID-19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in
person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This way the public, the staff,
and the Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which
are not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although
no action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak
during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to
speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and
follow the directions for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are
not subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been
submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public
comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Subject:  Malibu Arts Budget

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the Proposed Malibu Arts Budget for Fiscal Year
2023-2024; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION: The City's Annual Budget covers the period of July 1 to June 30 and serves
as a financial guide in providing services to the community based on the City Council's
Annual Work Plan. The operating budget is organized by department, then by program,
including narratives to explain the program's detail, purpose, and goals for the next year.

The Malibu Arts Budget (Arts Budget) includes funding for the Poet Laureate program, Art
Exhibitions, and Arts in Education (Attachment 1). The Arts Budget is funded from the
General Fund Undesignated Reserve, which are funds used to account for all assets and
liabilities not funded through Revenue, County, State, or Grant funds.

The Proposed Arts Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 (Attachment 2) includes art events,
programs, and exhibitions. Additional expenses include requests by the Poet Laureate
Committee, expansion of art exhibitions, and a general increase in operating and
contractor costs. The Malibu Arts budget is separated into several categories based on
the type of expense.

Salaries & Benefits
Expenditures are related to City personnel, including salaries, benefits, and full and part-
time compensation. The amount of funding allocated to full-time staff in the Arts Budget is
based on the estimated percentage of time spent by staff on arts-related programs.

Contract Personnel
Expenditures for services performed by personnel from temporary agencies or through a
limited contract with the City. These include instructors, performers, vendors, caterers,
and other contractors. All contract personnel costs related to the Arts in Education program
are included in this section and the Malibu Poet Laureate annual stipend. The Malibu Poet
Laureate Committee is requesting an increase in instructor stipends and an editor for the

to perform at six art exhibitions. A decrease of $8,000 includes completing poetry

purchases rights for public performance licensing to preview films legally. The licensing
satisfies federal copyright requirements.
Current Budget: $1,000
Proposed Budget FY 23-24: $1,000

Advertising & Noticing
Expenditures associated with arts programming and events related to advertising and
noticing. These include newspaper and virtual advertisements, banners, signs, and other
marketing materials. This section also includes funding for printing the annual Student
Poetry Anthology.
Current Budget: $12,000
Proposed Budget FY 23-24: $12,000

Operating Supplies
Expenses related to general operations of programs and events, including refreshments,
paper supplies, installation hardware, and other basic supplies. The Poet Laureate
Committee requested the installation of poetry displays for the Verse About Town
program. Additions include quarterly poetry readings, expansion from four budgeted art
exhibitions to six, and increases related to goods for all art events.
Current Budget: $21,700
Proposed Budget FY 23-24: $30,000

Revenues are included in the Annual Budget; however, the Arts Budget does not generate
revenues, as participants and artists are not charged a fee to attend or participate in
programs and events.

   MALIBU ARTS

The Community Services Department works with the Malibu Arts Commission to coordinate and
produce several art-related programs and projects within the Malibu community.

The Arts in Education program benefits local schools and features various speakers from different
artistic backgrounds and art workshops for children across all grade levels. The program has
provided students with insight into potential careers and creative expression they may not have
otherwise received through existing school programs.

The Malibu Poet Laureate program remains strong and continues to expand. The City appointed
its fourth Poet Laureate, Ann Buxie, who will serve a two-year term through October 2023. The
Poet Laureate works with members of the Poetry Laureate Committee to conduct poetry
programs, writing workshops, and open-mic events for adults. The Poet Laureate plans to curate
a Community Anthology and select poetry stones for Legacy Park at the conclusion of her term.
Former Malibu Poet Laureate Ricardo Means Ybarra continues to engage with student poets
through the Arts in Education program, and the City will once again publish the Annual Student
Poetry and Art Anthology in Fiscal Year 2022-2023. The Poet Laureate Committee also
collaborates with community partners such as the Malibu Library and Pepperdine University to
promote literary arts. Staff is currently evaluating options and opportunities to address expanded
investments in the Arts.

Art Exhibitions have included acclaimed artists in addition to displaying community artists in the
Malibu City Gallery located at City Hall. The Arts Commission is working toward exhibiting
exclusive works by world-renowned artists in Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

Arts programs and events resumed during Fiscal Year 2021-2022 following the COVID-19
Pandemic. Many arts programs and events are expected to fully resume as COVID-19 restrictions
are eased during Fiscal Year 2022-2023. As in 2021-22, a portion of the Recreation Coordinator
will be funded by the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA).

Subject:  Malibu Arts Center Survey Results

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review and discuss the results of the Malibu Arts Center
Survey; and 2) Provide a recommendation regarding the Malibu Arts Center for City
Council consideration.

DISCUSSION: The Commission was given an assignment by the City Council to explore
the potential for a performing arts center in Malibu. The Commission discussed several
options for the Malibu Arts Center at the Regular meetings on February 22, 2022, March
22, 2022, May 24, 2022, August 23, 2022, September 27, 2022, and October 25, 2022,
and November 22, 2022, in addition to the Special Meeting on March 10, 2022.

On November 22, 2022, the Commission approved the draft survey questions and
requested staff work with Chair Cherin and Commissioner Holland to finalize it before
distribution. The Malibu Arts Center Survey (Survey) was released to gauge the
community’s interest and preferred art-related amenities.

On December 22, 2022, the Survey was released to the public and was publicized on the
City’s social media platforms, and notifications were sent through the City’s email
database and added to the City Manager’s bi-weekly community message. The Survey
closed on February 6, 2023, and yielded 512 responses, including 441 responses from
residents of Malibu. Key information from the Survey included:

   95% of respondents want an Arts Center in Malibu
   407 respondents requested a theater/auditorium to be incorporated into the Malibu
  Arts Center
   The highest number of exhibitions people would attend include film screenings, art
  exhibitions, live theater shows, and local music events

    341 respondents stated a combination of private individuals and the City of Malibu
  should pay for the Malibu Arts Center

  REGULAR MEETING
  FEBRUARY 28, 2023
  TELECONFERENCED - VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  9:00A.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Cherin called the meeting to order at 9:03 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lotte Cherin; Vice Chair Fireball Lawrence; Commissioners BatTy
  Haldeman, Julia Holland, Peter Jones; and Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Acting Community Services Director; and Kate Gallo,
  Recreation Manager

  Vice Chair Lawrence led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION STATEMENT

  Commissioner Jones read the City of Malibu Vision Statement.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recreation Manager Gallo reported the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  February 24, 2023.

  John Mazza stated communication between the Parks and Recreation Commission
  and Planning Commission were essential to understand priorities, zoning issues,
  and restrictions before proposing an Arts Center.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked Mr. Mazza for his comments.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  I.  Arts in Education

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops were
  held at all Malibu schools in the Santa-Monica Malibu Unified School
  District. She stated staff were compiling poems and artist agreements for
  the 2023 Student Poetry and Art Anthology.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Commissioner Holland stated the spring art exhibition would include
  artwork by Jane Seymour. She stated the Commission would host a closing
  reception in June 2023.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the Jane Seymour exhibition would have
  freestanding pieces. He stated the Pep Williams art exhibition opening
  reception would take place on March 26, 2023 at 12:00 PM and the event
  included live music and a temporary display of artwork by Malibu Arts
  Association. He stated he worked with staff to install new gallery signs.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the Public Works Commission discussed a
  Neighborhood Beautification Program during the January 25, 2023 Regular
  meeting. He stated he would work with staff to obtain additional
  information on the Art in Public Places Ordinance.

  4.  Social Media

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked staff for consistent postings on social media.

  5.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the City Attorney was reviewing the
  Cooperative Agreement, which must be done before City Council approves
  the project.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu Arts Budget
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Proposed Malibu Arts Budget for Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Vice Chair Lawrence stated artists should
  select their frames and pay for framing expenses if they want their work showcased
  in the Malibu City Gallery.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Vice Chair Lawrence.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Chair Cherin stated the Commission could
  request additional funding from City Council at mid-year.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the Commission and staff had successfully worked
  within the parameters of the current budget.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staffing allocations were determined by City management. She stated poetry
  broadsides were Poet Laureate poems with a visual art element. She stated the Poet

  Laureate hosted quarterly poetry events typically with an open mic session and a
  featured reader, and poetry would be displayed in City parks.

  B.  Malibu Arts Center Survey Results
  Recommended Action: 1) Review and discuss the results of the Malibu Arts Center
  Survey; and 2) Provide a recommendation regarding the Malibu Arts Center for
  City Council consideration.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the Arts Center was not on 2022-2023 City Council work plan. She stated City
  Council planned to discuss 2023-2024 priorities at a Special meeting on March 22,
  2023. She stated the recommendation provided by the Commission would be
  provided to City Council for consideration.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Acting Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the City Council Special meeting on March 22, 2023 was open to the
  public.

  John Mazza stated the Arts Center was not on the City Council work plan because
  it was not a priority, and the project should be reviewed by City Council and the
  Planning Commission.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked Mr. Mazza for his comments and requested him to
  submit recommendations on ways to progress the Arts Center project.

  Mr. Mazza stated the survey results were one-sided and a professional surveyor was
  needed for a proper community study.

  Ex-Officio Clifford indicated disagreement with Mr. Mazza. He stated the initial
  low-cost survey was needed to determine a general consensus for City Council
  consideration.

  Commissioner Holland stated the Commission distributed the survey to gather
  initial information for City Council consideration. She stated the survey served its
  purpose to begin the discussion of an Arts Center.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Commissioner Holland.

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Vice Chair Lawrence seconded a motion to provide City

  called, and the motion catTied unanimously.
